life_summary: Thomas Spencer Monson was born August 21, 1927, at St. Mark's Hospital in Salt Lake City, Utah, to a respected family in the church community. He attended the University of Utah, where he majored in business administration, developing skills in leadership, organization, and practical management. Monson worked as a manager for the Deseret News Publishing Company, where he gained experience in media, publishing, and organizational administration. Throughout his secular career, Monson was known for his character, attention to detail, and genuine concern for individual people. His professional background in publishing and business management provided practical experience in communication and institutional leadership that served him well in ecclesiastical roles. He maintained strong connections to his Salt Lake City community and family throughout his life.
church_summary: Monson served as mission president to the Canadian Mission (Ontario and Quebec) from April 1959 to January 1962, overseeing 130–180 missionaries. Ordained an apostle in 1963, he advanced through leadership positions and became counselor to church presidents before his election as president in 2008, following Gordon B. Hinckley's death. As church president from 2008 to 2014, Monson led the denomination through major transitions and established fourteen new temple dedications and four rededications, including Rexburg Idaho, Draper Utah, Oquirrh Mountain Utah, Gilbert Arizona, and Phoenix Arizona temples. His ministry emphasized faith, service, spiritual development, and compassionate action. Monson was known for personal warmth and genuine care for individual members.
